claude.rationale: The company assembled the customer-facing portfolio (T4: 546 retail, 76 hotel, industrial, office and multi-family properties; the $841.8M Winston Hotels whole-company merger) onto its own balance sheet, but the operating processes that produce/deliver these assets did not cross with them: "Property-level operating processes were not run by the company's own organization," and it relied on affiliated property managers, a business manager, and IREA for acquisition identification — a product-vs-process mismatch at closing driving gap_45=1. Because T5 processes and T6 people/management sat together with the same sponsor affiliates (executive officers were employees of Inland Group affiliates; day-to-day operations under the business management agreement), the processes and the organization that run them stayed coherently aligned with each other, so gap_56=0. The gap_45 mismatch was contractually absorbed via the property-management, business-management, and property-acquisition agreements allocating the shared operating substrate (property management fees of $14,328K paid; IREA acquisition flow allocation), so gap_mitigated=yes.

gemini.rationale: The company acquired numerous real estate assets (T4) but did not acquire the operational processes (T5) or the people (T6) to run them, creating a structural gap between T4 and T5. This gap was mitigated at closing through property management and business management agreements with affiliates of the sponsor.

openai.rationale: The registrant assembled ownership interests in a large portfolio, including 100% of Winston's common and preferred stock, while property management, business operations, and acquisition identification remained with sponsor affiliates rather than transferring into the registrant. This documents a product-versus-process boundary mismatch at closing, but property-management, business-management, and property-acquisition agreements contractually bridged that shared operating substrate. The people running those external processes likewise remained with the affiliated managers, so the slice does not document a separate mismatch between transferred processes and their operating organization.
